animals.blurb: Named for their beautiful blue claws (red-tipped in females), blue crabs are a culinary icon of the Chesapeake Bay. They are aggressive fighters and strong swimmers.
animals.hint: An aggressive swimmer with beautiful blue claws

animals.habitat: Sandy and muddy seafloors, eelgrass beds
animals.blurb: Named after Dungeness, Washington, this crab is the most commercially important on the Pacific coast. They can reach 10 inches across and are prized for their sweet meat.
animals.hint: The sweet-meated king of the Pacific coast

animals.blurb: An icon of New England cuisine, American lobsters can live over 100 years and weigh over 40 pounds. They were once so abundant they were considered poverty food and fed to prisoners.
animals.hint: New England's ancient icon that was once prison food

animals.habitat: Coral reefs, rocky areas, seagrass beds
animals.blurb: Unlike true lobsters, spiny lobsters lack large claws but have long, spiny antennae. They migrate in remarkable single-file lines of up to 60 individuals marching across the seafloor.
animals.hint: A clawless lobster that marches in single file

animals.habitat: Swamps, ponds, slow streams, rice paddies
animals.blurb: The crawdad of Cajun cuisine, these hardy crayfish thrive in muddy waters and can survive droughts by burrowing. They have become invasive outside their native range.
animals.hint: The muddy Cajun delicacy that digs burrows

animals.blurb: Named for the white patches on their claws used in signaling, these large western crayfish are native to Pacific Northwest streams. They carry crayfish plague deadly to European species.
animals.hint: A western crayfish that signals with white claw patches

animals.blurb: These small crabs protect their soft abdomens by living in abandoned snail shells. As they grow, they must find larger shells, sometimes forming 'vacancy chains' where crabs swap shells in sequence.
animals.hint: A shell-swapping wanderer upgrading homes constantly

animals.blurb: Not actually crabs but ancient relatives of spiders, horseshoe crabs have remained virtually unchanged for 450 million years. Their blue blood is used to test medical equipment for contamination.
animals.hint: A living fossil with medically valuable blue blood

animals.blurb: Also called roly-polies, these are actually terrestrial crustaceans, not insects. They curl into balls when threatened and breathe through gill-like structures that must stay moist.
animals.hint: A land-dwelling crustacean that rolls into a ball

animals.blurb: Nearly transparent shrimp common in brackish waters. They are critical food for fish and birds and popular as fishing bait. Their clear bodies make their internal organs visible.
animals.hint: A see-through shrimp showing its inner workings
